brief: Morgan Stanley maps $1.6 trillion of 2027 hyperscaler and neocloud capex (cash capex plus new lease-capex estimates, which add $195bn) to single-stock supplier revenue. The new lease modeling raises 2026 capex to $980bn (+100% y/y), 2027 to $1.58-1.6T (+60% y/y) and 2028 to $1.8T (+14% y/y). An estimated 65% absorption rate means this capex adds 5% of 2027 S&P 500 sales and drives about 25% of S&P 500 sales growth, with NVDA capturing nearly $700bn of the $1.0T that reaches the index. Beyond direct capex mapping, a broader 42-name AI cohort is growing 2027 sales 28% versus 5% for non-AI peers and driving 78% of 2027 S&P 500 earnings growth. Financing needs are expected to rise in 2027 as the hyperscaler cash-flow deficit widens, though MS judges AA-rated hyperscalers price-insensitive to higher rates while lower-rated borrowers face tighter constraints. A Powering AI model projects a 32 GW US power shortfall through 2028, which could delay energization rather than cut chip demand. Midterm-election outcomes are flagged as a secondary political risk to the data-center buildout.
